title: Burns Anaesthesia Fellowship
inst: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre
Department: Department of Anesthesia, Sunnybrook / University of Toronto Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine
Duration: 12 months (shorter or longer may be pursued under certain circumstances)
Deadline: Apply at least 15 months in advance; January 2027 session closed; online forms open for July 2027 and January 2028 intakes
Eligibility: Minimum 30 months of clinical anaesthesia training and all requisite certification exams passed in home country; preference for training completed within past seven years; fluency in English mandatory
International applicants: Yes — open to international graduates; applicants whose first language is not English must pass TOEFL/TSE or IELTS
Accreditation: University of Toronto PGME-registered fellowship; does not count towards Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada specialty certification

Summary: A one-year fellowship focused on perioperative anaesthetic management and ICU care of patients with burn injuries at the Ross Tilley Burn Centre, the largest burn care centre in Canada.

Department: Department of Emergency Medicine, University of Ottawa
Duration: 1 year (2 years combined with MSc Clinical Epidemiology)
Deadline: 1 September for July start; 1 February for January start
Eligibility: EM-certified physicians eligible for independent practice in Ontario, FRCPC EM residents in subspecialty year, or international applicants with EM certification

Accreditation: RCPSC Area of Focused Competence (AFC) Diploma programme
Application method: CV, letter of interest and 3 references via uOttawa fellowship application (IMGs via international graduates process)
Funding: Institution policy: international fellows without Canadian status must be funded by an official home-country sponsor (government agency or health-related charity; private funds not accepted) unless fellowship funding is available through an Ottawa hospital

title: Prehospital and Transport Medicine AFC Diploma Program

Application method: Letter of interest, CV and 3 references via uOttawa fellowship application system
Funding: Institution policy: international fellows without Canadian status must be funded by an official home-country sponsor (government agency or health-related charity; private funds not accepted) unless fellowship funding is available through an Ottawa hospital

title: Medical Education Fellowship
inst: University of Ottawa / The Ottawa Hospital

Summary: A clinician-educator fellowship scaffolding a Master's in medical/health professions education, run jointly with the Centre for Innovation in Medical Education.

title: Acute Care Point-of-Care Ultrasound (AFC) Fellowship
inst: University of British Columbia
Department: Department of Emergency Medicine, UBC (VGH, Royal Columbian and St. Paul's Hospitals)

Eligibility: Resident in a Canadian Royal College EM programme or board-certified EM physician (FRCPC-EM or CCFP-EM)
International applicants: Institution policy (UBC PGME): international doctors may train as Postgraduate Fellows if they have completed all specialist training/exams in their home country (letter from home specialty college required), meet CPSBC English requirements and have a written Training Agreement; government-sponsored visa trainees apply via agencies with a UBC agreement
Accreditation: RCPSC Area of Focused Competence (AFC) Diploma in Acute Care Point-of-Care Ultrasonography
Application method: Departmental application form; interview in person or by phone
Funding: Institution policy (UBC PGME): fellows are not covered by the Resident Doctors of BC agreement; a written Training Agreement with the sponsoring Health Authority/University sets pay; $500 PGME administrative fee plus annual CPSBC licence fee; self-funded or unfunded postgraduate trainees are not eligible
Visa support: Institution policy (UBC PGME): foreign trainees must hold an IRCC work permit for the whole training period; the sponsoring department/PGME submits an offer of employment to IRCC and the fellow applies under the LMIA-exempt category
Licence requirement: Hold or be eligible for CPSBC registration and CMPA liability coverage
Summary: A nine-month multi-site AFC POCUS fellowship training emergency physicians to lead POCUS in urban and rural Canada, with 700–800 scans, teaching and programme development.

title: Emergency Medicine Point-of-Care Ultrasound Fellowship
inst: University of Calgary (Cumming School of Medicine)

Eligibility: Resident or fellow in a Canadian Royal College programme, or Canadian board-certified physician (FRCP or CCFP-EM)
International applicants: Institution policy: International medical graduates accepted as International Clinical Fellows or Sponsored Fellows if they hold a CPSA-acceptable medical degree, completed residency, verify credentials via physiciansapply.ca, meet CPSA English-language requirements and obtain a work permit; funding must come from a PGME-approved source
Application method: Send CV and cover letter to the programme
Funding: Institution policy: No PGME funding; clinical fellows must be funded by a PGME-approved source (department/AHS/sponsoring government, hospital or university - no personal funds), with stipend at least equivalent to PGY1 under the Alberta Resident Physician Agreement

Licence requirement: Eligibility and registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta; medical liability insurance
Summary: A one-year POCUS fellowship preparing graduates to lead an academic or community emergency ultrasound programme, sufficient to meet ARDMS certification requirements.
